title: Position FAAB calibration blends RAW dollar bids from three seasons with different budgets ($1000 / $200 / $100), inflating the RB anchor 5.0x and driving every bid too high
claimUnderTest: faab_analytics.py docstring: 'calibrates the per-player FAAB recommendation against the league's actual historical winning bids for similar position+tier so the recommendation reflects how THIS league bids'. _league_budget() reads 'the current season's waiver_budget setting'.
observed: _walk_waivers() flattens EVERY season's transactions into one bid list with no budget normalization, while _league_budget() returns only the CURRENT season's budget. The live snapshot covers 2026 (waiver_budget=100), 2025 (200) and 2024 (1000). positionBids['RB'].avg is therefore $43.00 -- a mean over bids denominated in three different currencies, with a max of $340 which is physically impossible in a $100 league. recommend_faab blends that number 50/50 into every RB bid on a $100 budget.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.public_league import snapshot_store;s=snapshot_store.load_snapshot();[print(x.season,(getattr(x,'league',{}) or {}).get('settings',{}).get('waiver_budget')) for x in s.seasons]" && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/faabAnalytics?leagueKey=dynasty_main' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['positionBids'])"
reproduction.expected: Position averages expressed as a share of the season each bid was placed in, i.e. RB ~ $8.58 on a $100 budget
reproduction.actual: 2026 budget=100, 2025 budget=200, 2024 budget=1000; positionBids RB {'avg': 43.0, 'min': 1, 'max': 340, 'count': 53}; league max bid $340 on a $100 budget

numericProof.formula: normalized_bid = raw_bid / season_budget * 100 ; RB_anchor = mean(normalized_bids) ; recommended = 0.5*RB_anchor + 0.5*baseline

userImpact: Every RB waiver bid on /waivers is anchored to a number 5x larger than the league's own budget-normalized history. A user is told to bid $22-$32 of a $100 budget on replacement-level running backs. This is the single largest contributor to the reported 'FAAB recommendations are too aggressive'.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set. PRIOR-A04-F08 noticed tierBids was unused but not that positionBids itself mixes budget regimes. Note the irony: src/adapters/ktc_crowd_faab.py::_parse_bid_pct DOES normalize by waiver_budget 'so multi-budget leagues normalize correctly' -- the league's own history is the one place it is skipped.

whatWorks: The multi-add split at full precision (faab_analytics.py:240-246) and the tier breakpoints scaling with league_budget are both correct.
rootCause: _league_budget() is scalar and current-season-only; _walk_waivers() is multi-season. The two are combined without a per-season divisor.
requiredRepair: Carry the season's waiver_budget alongside each bid in _walk_waivers, express every bid as a share of its own season's budget, and re-multiply by the CURRENT budget before it reaches positionBids / leagueAvgWinningBid / leagueMedianWinningBid / teamAggression.
dependencies: Fixing this alone drops RB recommendations from ~$32 to ~$15 and unpriced-RB recommendations from $22 to $4; W11-F002 must be fixed too or the unpriced case survives at a lower number.

title: Players the board declines to price (rankDerivedValue = 0) are recommended $22-$25 bids and described as a 'strong free-agent target'; 125 of 283 free agents are affected
claimUnderTest: _compute_faab_bid: 'if candidate_value <= 0 or budget <= 0: return (0, 0, 0)'. faab_recommender module docstring: 'Missing data is never imputed into a normal-looking value'.
observed: The zero guard fires correctly and the baseline factor row honestly reads 'Player value baseline: start at $0'. Step 4 then blends that $0 against the position's historical average -- 0.5*avg + 0.5*0 -- and resurrects a bid out of nothing. The explanation string is chosen only on the magnitude of the final number, so a player worth 0 gets 'strong free-agent target'. Rival contention can then raise it further: Zach Wilson (value 0) received '+$6 to clear top rival'.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"AJ Dillon","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"468418790212759552"}'
reproduction.expected: standard 0, or an explicit 'we do not price this player' response
reproduction.actual: {"conservative":15,"standard":22,"aggressive":31,"resolvedAddValue":0.0,"explanation":"Bid $22 - strong free-agent target.  Cap at $31 if you want the priority claim."}

userImpact: On /waivers a manager is told to spend 22% of the season budget on a player this product's own board refuses to value, with no warning and with copy calling it a strong target. The recommendation is a pure function of position, not of the player.

priorFinding.note: 125 of the 283 unrostered contract rows carry rankDerivedValue = 0 and 125 of those receive a non-zero bid; the observed bid set is {2,4,7,10,22,25} keyed entirely off position.

whatWorks: The 15 zero-value rows whose contract row also carries no position (e.g. Foster Moreau) DO correctly return $0 -- the calibration is skipped when position is None.
rootCause: _position_calibration is an unconditional blend on the running bid; nothing re-checks that the baseline was a real number rather than the zero-guard's sentinel.
requiredRepair: Short-circuit recommend_faab when add_player_value <= 0 and return an explicit unpriced response (mirroring the BDVM 'unpriced with a reason' posture), or gate every post-baseline multiplier/blend on reasonable_base > 0.
dependencies: Independent of W11-F001, but F001 sets the magnitude.

title: The bid saturates at the top of the FREE-AGENT pool, so 367 board rows (value >= 1908) price identically and no player anywhere justifies more than 40% of the budget -- there is no all-in threshold
claimUnderTest: User's stated calibration intent: a ~9999 player justifies the whole budget, and the all-in threshold should sit far below the top of the dynasty market (near J.K. Dobbins / Jaylen Warren, not Josh Jacobs). frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:858-860 documents 'a 9999-value player gets 30% of the budget'.
observed: share = candidate_value / max(candidate_value, top_value_in_pool), so every player at or above the best available free agent has share = 1.0 and an identical baseline. On the live board the top free agent is Marlin Klein (1908, board rank 325), so Josh Allen (9988), Josh Jacobs (3859), Jaylen Warren (2937), J.K. Dobbins (2660) and Marlin Klein all take exactly the same $30/$21/$11 baseline. Sweeping the endpoint over all 283 free agents returns a maximum standard bid of $31; sweeping the top 200 of the whole board returns a maximum of $40. Nothing on the board triggers an all-in bid, and the number does not scale with the 1..9999 axis at all above rank 325.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Josh Allen","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"468418790212759552"}' && for N in 'Josh Jacobs' 'Jaylen Warren' 'J.K. Dobbins' 'Marlin Klein'; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"addPlayerName\":\"$N\",\"leagueKey\":\"dynasty_main\",\"teamOwnerId\":\"468418790212759552\"}"; echo; done   # full board sweep archived at docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/board-top200-sweep.json
reproduction.expected: Josh Allen (9988) near the full $100 budget; a Dobbins/Warren-class asset (2660-2937) at the all-in threshold; Marlin Klein (1908) well below it
reproduction.actual: Josh Allen standard $38 / aggressive $53; Josh Jacobs $32; Jaylen Warren $32; J.K. Dobbins $32; Marlin Klein $15. Maximum standard over the top 200 board rows = $40 (Malik Willis, value 3684).

numericProof.formula: share = v / max(v, 1908); aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25*share; reasonable = roundHalfUp(100*pct*0.70)

userImpact: The bid desk cannot express 'this is a league-winner, empty the budget' or 'this is roster filler, bid $1'. It compresses the entire dynasty market into a $12-$40 band, so the user cannot rank waiver targets by the recommendation and over-pays at the bottom while under-paying at the top.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and extended. The prior finding measured _compute_faab_bid(1905,100,1905) = (30,21,10) in isolation; this reproduces the same saturation end-to-end through the live endpoint, counts the 367 affected board rows, and measures the actual ceiling ($40 over the top 200) against the user's stated intent. The lowball figure is 11 not 10 -- the rounding rule changed to explicit half-up since that measurement.

whatWorks: The denominator is now correctly restricted to non-pick free agents (server.py:5130), which is what makes 1908 the anchor.
rootCause: The formula answers 'what fraction of the best available free agent is this player' and prints a dollar sign on it. Its output range is structurally [5%, 30%] of budget regardless of the absolute quality of the pool.
requiredRepair: Replace the pool-relative share with an absolute mapping from the 1..9999 board scale to a share of budget, with an explicitly calibrated all-in knee. The user's stated intent puts the knee near value ~2700-2950 (Dobbins/Warren), i.e. board rank ~180-210, not at Josh Jacobs (3859, rank 109).
dependencies: Interacts with W11-F001 (the position blend currently dominates the baseline) and W11-F005 (the client hint uses the same formula with a different denominator).

title: The recommendation is not monotonic in player value: 8,362 of 39,903 free-agent pairs invert, worst case a $21 swing in favour of the lower-valued player
claimUnderTest: Implied by the product: a better player should not be assigned a lower recommended bid than a worse one.
observed: Because the position blend (weight 0.5) and the trending kicker (up to x1.20) both sit downstream of the only value-sensitive term, position and Sleeper add-count routinely dominate value. Measured over all 283 free agents at a fixed budget/roster: 8,362 inverted pairs (21.0% of all pairs).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;o=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/fa-pool-sweep.json'));v=sum(1 for i in range(len(o)) for j in range(i+1,len(o)) if o[i]['value']>o[j]['value'] and o[i]['standard']<o[j]['standard']);print(v,'of',len(o)*(len(o)-1)//2)"
reproduction.expected: 0 inversions
reproduction.actual: 8362 of 39903 pairs inverted. Worst: Zion Young (DL, value 1447) -> $10 vs Seth McGowan (RB, value 1383) -> $31. On the full board: Malik Willis (3684) -> $40 vs Josh Allen (9988) -> $38.

userImpact: A manager comparing two waiver targets side by side is told to bid three times more on the worse one. The recommendation cannot be used to prioritise claims, which is its primary job.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding argued the formula is not a bid; this quantifies the consequence with a full pairwise sweep, which the prior set did not measure.

whatWorks: Within a single position the ordering IS monotonic -- the inversions are entirely cross-position (plus the trending kicker).
rootCause: A 0.5-weight additive blend on a position constant is applied after the value term, so it can exceed the value term's entire dynamic range.
requiredRepair: Make the league calibration a MULTIPLIER on the value bid rather than a 50/50 blend with a position constant, so ordering within the value axis is preserved.
dependencies: W11-F001 (the position constants are themselves inflated) and W11-F010 (they are means of a skewed distribution).

title: The /waivers 'FAAB hint' column changes the recommended dollar bid for the same player when the user changes the position filter -- Charlie Kolar $19 under 'All positions', $21 under 'TE'
claimUnderTest: Column header tooltip: 'Quick baseline share of a $100 budget - use the bid desk for a league-aware recommendation.'
observed: topAddValue is the maximum add value among the CURRENTLY DISPLAYED bestMoves rows, and it is the denominator of computeFaabHint's share. Changing the position dropdown changes the visible set, which changes the denominator, which changes the printed dollar figure for players whose own value did not change. By construction the top row of the column always reads $21.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/repro_waivers_page.py   # Playwright with /api/* request interception per AUDIT_PROTOCOL; selects team 'Jason', reads the Best add/drop moves table under filters ALL / QB / RB / TE
reproduction.expected: identical hint for the same player under every filter
reproduction.actual: Charlie Kolar: $19 (All positions) -> $21 (TE). Mitchell Evans: $18 -> $20. Under every filter the #1 row prints $21 (Jonas Sanker, Joe Milton, George Holani, Charlie Kolar).

userImpact: A UI filter that is supposed to narrow a list silently re-prices every bid in it. A manager who filters to TE is told to bid $21 on a player the unfiltered view priced at $19, and the top row is always $21 no matter how bad the pool is.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A04-F02 is about the hint disagreeing with the bid desk (see W11-F007). This is the hint disagreeing with ITSELF across a display filter, which the prior set did not test. Measured in a real browser through request interception.

whatWorks: computeFaabHint itself is a faithful port of the server formula (see W11-F020).
rootCause: The denominator is computed from the filtered render list (page.jsx topAddValue memo) instead of from the whole addable pool.
requiredRepair: Compute topAddValue once from the unfiltered addable pool (or, better, drop the pool-relative share entirely per W11-F003) and pass the league's real budget rather than a literal 100.
dependencies: Shares the root formula with W11-F003.

title: The /waivers league FAAB context panel unwraps the wrong envelope key (data.body vs the API's data.data), so every league bid statistic renders as an em dash despite the API returning real numbers
claimUnderTest: In-code comment at ManualAddDrop.jsx:308: 'The /api/public/league/{section} endpoint wraps the builder output as ``{section, body}`` so unwrap.'
observed: The live endpoint returns {contractVersion, league, section, data}. There is no 'body' key, so `data?.body || data` falls through to the whole envelope and every field read (leagueBudget, leagueAvgWinningBid, leagueMedianWinningBid, positionBids, playerHistory) is undefined. Because the envelope is truthy the panel still RENDERS -- it does not take the documented 'stays hidden' path -- so the user sees a populated-looking panel full of em dashes.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/faabAnalytics?leagueKey=dynasty_main' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print('top',list(d.keys()));print('has body',\"body\" in d);print('avg',d['data']['leagueAvgWinningBid'],'median',d['data']['leagueMedianWinningBid'])"  # then load /waivers via Playwright request interception and read the FAAB strip
reproduction.expected: LEAGUE AVERAGE BID $20 / LEAGUE MEDIAN BID $5
reproduction.actual: API returns leagueAvgWinningBid 19.55, leagueMedianWinningBid 5.0, totalBidsAnalyzed 302; the rendered page shows 'LEAGUE AVERAGE BID -- winning bids' and 'LEAGUE MEDIAN BID -- winning bids'

userImpact: The only place on /waivers that would let a manager sanity-check a $22 recommendation against their league's actual $5 median bid is blank. The comparable-position and per-player bid history blocks are dead for the same reason, so the recommendation is presented with no context at all.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set; PRIOR-A04-F05 assumed leagueFaab.leagueBudget was available to the hint, which it is not.

whatWorks: The backend builder and the Next bridge route are both correct; only the client-side unwrap is wrong.
rootCause: The comment and the code were written against a {section, body} envelope the route does not produce.
requiredRepair: `setLeagueFaab(data?.data || data?.body || null)`. Also note the route signature takes only `owner` and `refresh`, so the `?leagueKey=` the client sends is silently ignored -- the panel is not league-scoped.

title: Two different FAAB dollar figures for the same player render on /waivers at once and disagree by up to 75%
claimUnderTest: Both numbers are presented as this product's recommended FAAB bid for the same player, in the same league, on the same screen.
observed: The Best-add/drop-moves table's 'FAAB hint' uses computeFaabHint with a $100 literal budget and the filtered-batch maximum as denominator. The bid desk uses the server recommend_faab with the whole-free-agent-pool maximum plus the position calibration, trending kicker and contention. Neither knows about the other.

reproduction.command: # Table value: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/repro_waivers_page.py ; Desk value: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Harold Landry","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"468418790212759552"}'
reproduction.expected: one number
reproduction.actual: Harold Landry: table $21, desk $12 (75% apart). Jonas Sanker: $21 vs $16. Charlie Kolar: $19 vs $15. Mack Wilson: $18 vs $11.

userImpact: A manager reads $21 in the table, clicks the same player into the calculator immediately below it, and is told $12. There is no indication which is authoritative.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced end-to-end in a browser plus the live endpoint. The prior finding measured $21 vs $12 for Mitchell Evans on team Blaine; I measure the same 75% gap for Harold Landry on team Jason, so the magnitude is stable across teams. The prior finding attributed the desk side to a pick-contaminated denominator -- that part is now fixed (see W11-F019) and the disagreement survives anyway.

whatWorks: The header tooltip does say 'use the bid desk for a league-aware recommendation', which is a partial disclosure.
rootCause: Two independent implementations of the same product concept with different denominators and different budgets.
requiredRepair: Delete the client-side hint column and render the server number, or batch-call the recommender for the visible rows.

title: The value-gain modifier is inverted with respect to the drop side: adding a player for free is recommended at $32 while adding the same player and dropping a worthless one is recommended at $40
claimUnderTest: _value_gain_modifier docstring: 'Bigger upgrade => higher modifier. Drop value of 0 (FA-only add, no drop required) returns 1.0 (no boost, no penalty).'
observed: The modifier is 1 + (add-drop)/drop * 0.5 clamped to [0.5, 1.8], and drop_value appears in the DENOMINATOR. A no-drop add is hard-coded to 1.0, but dropping a near-worthless player produces a ratio near infinity and clamps to 1.8. So the transaction that costs the manager an extra asset is priced 80% HIGHER than the same transaction that costs nothing.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/faab_axis_probe.py  # read out['dropSideSweep']
reproduction.expected: bid(no drop) >= bid(same add, plus a drop)
reproduction.actual: drop_value 0 -> $32; drop_value 500 -> $40; drop_value 2000 -> $37; drop_value 3858 -> $32; drop_value 3859 -> $10; drop_value 5000 -> $0

userImpact: Selecting a drop player -- something the UI encourages, since the calculator has a DROP side -- raises the recommended bid by up to 25% for the identical add. The manager pays more for a worse net transaction.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set.

whatWorks: The strictly-negative branch is right: add < drop returns $0 with 'Your drop is worth more than your add - don't bid.' Verified live at drop_value 5000 -> $0.
rootCause: Using drop_value as the denominator makes the modifier a function of how BAD the drop is rather than of how much the roster improves.
requiredRepair: Scale the modifier by net gain relative to the ADD's value (or to a replacement-level constant), not relative to the drop's value, and make the no-drop case the maximum rather than the neutral case.

title: FAAB v2's budget-environment scaling stage cannot fire for any position that has bid history -- it is dead code on live data
claimUnderTest: faab_recommender module docstring step 7: 'Budget-environment scaling (league bid temperature; skipped whenever step 4's per-position calibration already fired)'.
observed: The double-count guard suppresses env scaling whenever positionBids[pos].count >= 3. On the live league every position with any history has count >= 10 (QB 39, RB 53, WR 64, TE 26, DL 30, LB 39, DB 41, K 10), so _env_scale_factor returns None for all of them. It returns a non-None value only for positions with NO bid history (P, OL) or for a row with no position at all -- i.e. never for a real waiver add.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.trade.faab_recommender import _env_scale_factor;from src.api import faab_analytics;from src.public_league import snapshot_store;S=faab_analytics.summarize_league_faab(snapshot_store.load_snapshot());print({p:_env_scale_factor(S,p,100) for p in ('QB','RB','WR','TE','DL','LB','DB','K','P')})"
reproduction.expected: a scaling factor for at least some real positions
reproduction.actual: {'QB': None, 'RB': None, 'WR': None, 'TE': None, 'DL': None, 'LB': None, 'DB': None, 'K': None, 'P': 0.625}

numericProof.formula: env applies iff totalBidsAnalyzed >= 10 AND positionBids[pos].count < 3

userImpact: None directly -- but the module docstring, the factor list and the /waivers 'factors behind this bid' disclosure all present an eight-stage model of which one stage never runs. An operator tuning the recommender will tune a constant with no effect.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set.

whatWorks: The double-count guard itself is correct reasoning; it is the min-count threshold (3) that is set so low it swallows the whole feature.
rootCause: The precedence gate reuses _POSITION_CALIBRATION_MIN_COUNT = 3, which any active league clears for every position.
requiredRepair: Either delete the stage and the docstring claim, or change the precedence rule so env scaling applies to the residual after the position blend rather than being mutually exclusive with it.

title: The league calibration anchors on the MEAN of a heavily right-skewed winning-bid distribution (league mean $19.55 vs median $5.00), systematically biasing every recommendation upward
claimUnderTest: _position_calibration: 'Blend bid_estimate 50/50 with the league's historical average winning bid for position ... keeps the formula honest in leagues where users overpay'.
observed: _stats_block emits only avg/min/max/count -- no median -- and the recommender blends against avg. The live distribution is extremely skewed: league mean $19.55 vs median $5.00 (3.9x), RB mean $43.00 vs median $18.00, QB mean $37.74 vs median $6.00. The recommender therefore calibrates to the tail, not to the typical claim, and it does this on top of the cross-budget contamination in W11-F001. summarize_league_faab already computes leagueMedianWinningBid at league level -- the per-position block simply never got one.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/faabAnalytics?leagueKey=dynasty_main' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'];print('leagueMean',d['leagueAvgWinningBid'],'leagueMedian',d['leagueMedianWinningBid']);print(d['positionBids'])"
reproduction.expected: a robust central estimate for the position
reproduction.actual: leagueAvgWinningBid 19.55, leagueMedianWinningBid 5.0; positionBids carries only 'avg' -- QB avg 37.74 (median 6.00), RB avg 43.00 (median 18.00)

userImpact: Every bid is pulled halfway toward the mean of a distribution whose typical value is a quarter of that mean. Combined with W11-F001 this is why an unpriced QB is recommended at $25.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A04-F08 observed that tierBids is unused while the docstring claims position+tier calibration. This is the adjacent defect the prior set did not name: even within positionBids the statistic chosen is the wrong one.

whatWorks: leagueMedianWinningBid is computed correctly and IS used by the contention aggression factor.
rootCause: _stats_block was written for display (avg/min/max/count) and then reused as a calibration input.
requiredRepair: Add a 'median' (and ideally a trimmed mean) to _stats_block and calibrate against it.
dependencies: W11-F001 must be fixed first or the median is still denominated in three currencies.

title: The pacing warning only inspects the 'standard' bid, so the 'Aggressive' pill can offer 53% of the budget with no warning shown
claimUnderTest: faab_recommender docstring: 'plus a pacing warning whenever the standard bid exceeds 40% of the remaining budget ... so the user consciously accepts the season-long tradeoff'.
observed: aggressive = round(standard * 1.40) is rendered as a peer pill the user can act on, but the _PACING_WARN_SHARE check runs only against standard. Any standard between 29% and 40% produces an aggressive figure of 40-56% with an empty warnings array.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Josh Allen","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"468418790212759552"}'
reproduction.expected: a pacing warning on a bid worth more than 40% of the budget
reproduction.actual: {"standard":38,"aggressive":53,"max":100,"warnings":[]} -- 67 of the top 200 board rows and 11 of 283 free agents show aggressive > 40% of budget with an empty warnings array

userImpact: The pill the product labels 'Aggressive' is exactly the one a manager reaches for on a player they want, and it is the one the pacing guardrail does not cover.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set.

whatWorks: The cap itself holds: across 483 live endpoint calls, standard <= max and aggressive <= max in every case (0 violations).
rootCause: The warning was written against the single recommended number and never extended when the three-pill bracket was added.
requiredRepair: Evaluate the pacing share against the highest actionable pill, or attach a per-pill warning.

title: The 'Max' bid pill is labelled 'your remaining' even when the value is the league budget because the team could not be identified
claimUnderTest: UI: StatTile label 'Max', meta 'your remaining'.
observed: cap_source = team_faab_remaining if not None else league_budget, and max is that cap_source. team_faab_remaining is populated only when teamOwnerId matches a CURRENT roster AND the overlay resolved an integer faabRemaining. A request with no teamOwnerId returns max = 100 (the league budget) and the pill still reads 'your remaining'.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Marlin Klein","leagueKey":"dynasty_main"}' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print('max',d['max'],'contentionSkipped',d['contention']['skipped'])"
reproduction.expected: a null / 'unknown' max, or a differently-labelled tile
reproduction.actual: {"max": 100, "contentionSkipped": true} -- indistinguishable in the payload from a manager who genuinely has $100 left

numericProof.formula: max = team_faab_remaining if team_faab_remaining is not None else league_budget

userImpact: A manager who has spent most of their budget can be shown 'Max $100 - your remaining' and bid money they do not have. Nothing else on the panel distinguishes the two cases.

priorFinding.note: Code path unchanged; reproduced live. In this container the fallback is invisible because all 12 rosters report faabRemaining 100, so the harm requires a mid-season league to observe -- but the payload gives the client no way to tell the cases apart, which is the defect.

whatWorks: When teamOwnerId DOES match, the cap is applied correctly -- sweeping team_faab_remaining 100/50/20/5/1/0 never produced a bid above the balance (0 violations).
rootCause: The API returns a single 'max' with no provenance flag.
requiredRepair: Return maxSource: 'teamRemaining' | 'leagueBudget' (the payload already stamps provenance elsewhere, e.g. valuationMode) and let the pill label itself.

title: No FAAB input is sensitive to time of season, roster need, contender-vs-rebuilder posture, or whether the add is a temporary injury fill-in -- the bid is priced entirely on long-run DYNASTY value
claimUnderTest: The bid desk is presented as a league-aware FAAB recommendation.
observed: Grepping the whole FAAB path (waiver.py, faab_recommender.py, faab_contention.py, ktc_crowd_faab.py) for week / season / playoff / contender / rebuild / injur returns zero functional references -- only docstring prose. The single value input is rankDerivedValue, the dynasty market board. Positional need exists, but ONLY for modelling RIVAL bids (faab_contention.need_level_for); the requesting user's own roster need is never consulted. Consequence on the live board: the top of the free-agent pool is Marlin Klein, Tanner Koziol, Jack Endries and Sam Roush -- four deep-bench rookie TEs with dynasty upside -- while startable veteran RB depth (AJ Dillon, Alexander Mattison) prices at 0. The desk therefore steers the whole budget at players who will never enter a lineup.

reproduction.command: grep -nciE 'week|playoff|contend|rebuild|injur' src/trade/waiver.py src/trade/faab_recommender.py src/trade/faab_contention.py ; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/faab_axis_probe.py
reproduction.expected: at least one in-season / roster-context input
reproduction.actual: 0 functional references in all three modules. Axis probe: the ONLY inputs the output moves on are player value (saturating), position (via the historical blend), Sleeper trending count, drop-side value, rival clearing price and the team's remaining balance.

userImpact: A week-3 injury replacement a manager needs for four weeks and a durable dynasty asset are priced the same, and a rebuilding team is told to spend like a contender. A FAAB claim is a rest-of-season decision priced on a rest-of-career number.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding asserted this from code reading. I confirm it by axis-sweeping the live function and additionally show WHICH axes do move the number, and that league-wide remaining FAAB is unread (only per-rival balances, and only as a cap).

whatWorks: Rival-side positional need IS modelled (NEED_FACTORS 1.0/0.55/0.25) and does reach the clearing price.
rootCause: There is no rest-of-season value feed for the waiver pool. /api/ros/player-values covers only the top 500 board players; none of the 283 free agents (checked: AJ Dillon, Alexander Mattison, Marlin Klein, Jonas Sanker) appear in it.
requiredRepair: Two separable pieces: (a) thread current week + a contender/rebuilder posture into a budget-pacing multiplier, which needs no new data; (b) extend the ROS aggregation past the top 500 so free agents carry a rest-of-season value the bid can be priced on.

title: POST /api/waiver/suggestions has no caller and sizes its bids against the manager's REMAINING balance where the shared formula's own docstring says BUDGET
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'POST /api/waiver/suggestions | yes | no UI caller - /waivers computes client-side from contract rows'.
observed: Confirmed disconnected: no reference in frontend/ outside .next build output, and no Next bridge route under frontend/app/api/waiver/. The route is reachable and returns 200 with real data. It reads faabRemaining from the request body (default 100) and forwards it as budget= into _compute_faab_bid, so its bids are 30%/21%/10.5% of REMAINING while recommend_faab's identical call is a share of the league BUDGET capped at remaining. Same player, same league, two meanings.

reproduction.command: for B in 100 50 20 5 1 0; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/suggestions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"minValue\":500,\"faabRemaining\":$B}" | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['by_position']['TE'][0])"; done
reproduction.expected: bids that mean the same thing as the bid desk's
reproduction.actual: Marlin Klein reasonable: $21 at remaining 100, $11 at 50, $4 at 20, $1 at 5, $0 at 0. The desk for the same player at remaining $20 would say $21 capped to $20.

numericProof.formula: suggestions: reasonable = roundHalfUp(remaining*0.30*0.70) ; recommender: standard = f(budget=100) then min(., remaining)

userImpact: Zero today (no caller). Any future caller inherits a silently different definition of the same dollar figure.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with a live budget sweep the prior finding did not run. One correction: waiver.py no longer coerces a 0 balance to 100 -- the current code coerces only None, and a 0 balance correctly yields $0 bids across all positions (verified).

whatWorks: The two-source minimum (sourceCount >= 2) and the None-vs-zero balance distinction in find_waiver_targets are both correct and verified live.
rootCause: One helper, two callers, two meanings of its 'budget' argument -- documented in the docstring but not enforced.
requiredRepair: Delete the route, or rename the parameter at the call site and make the suggestions path share the recommender's budget semantics.

title: The rival-contention model reads the unscoped market contract while the user's own bid reads the valuation-lens-scoped one, and a single valuationMode is stamped for both
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Every response stamps valuationMode ... "This is the market board" and "this field is missing" must not read the same.'
observed: The handler threads the lens through _valuation_scoped_contract and uses the scoped arr for add/drop values, the pool max and the next-best-FA value, but passes the module-global latest_contract_data to estimate_rival_bids for both the opponent asset pool and the player-position map. Under valuation_mode='leagueAdjusted' the user's bid is priced on one board and rival need levels on another, and the response stamps one mode for both.

reproduction.command: grep -n '_valuation_scoped_contract\|contract=latest_contract_data\|player_position_map(latest_contract_data)' server.py | sed -n '1,20p'
reproduction.expected: the same board on both sides of the comparison
reproduction.actual: server.py:5038 uses the scoped contract for arr; server.py:5389 and 5369 pass latest_contract_data to the estimator

userImpact: Second-order: need levels are categorical (need/neutral/surplus) so the two boards usually agree. But the clearing price the user is told to beat is derived from a board the response does not name.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by code read against the current tree. Could not be exercised end-to-end here: the league-adjusted overlay requires a roster snapshot this container serves, and market mode is the default for the test user, so the divergence is structural rather than observed.

whatWorks: valuationMode IS stamped on the response, including 'market'.
rootCause: The estimator call was written before the lens threading landed and was not updated.
requiredRepair: Pass the scoped contract into estimate_rival_bids and player_position_map.

title: waiver-logic's rowValue falls back to values.full, which on the default payload is the raw scraper composite -- 4 of 57 roster rows on the live team are priced off a value the canonical pipeline declined to stamp
claimUnderTest: waiver-logic.js:197-199 'Prefer rankDerivedValue (the canonical 0-9999 stamp). Fall back to values.full which buildRows already prefers when the backend stamp is present anyway.'
observed: On the default view=app payload buildRows takes the legacy-dict branch where `full: backendValue || rawValues.full`, and rawValues.full is _finalAdjusted -- the raw scraper composite. So the fallback is not a synonym for the canonical stamp; it is a different number from a different pipeline. Measured on the live contract for team Jason: 4 of 57 roster rows carry rankDerivedValue null and a non-null _finalAdjusted (Devon Witherspoon 1935, Mason Graham 1874, Malaki Starks 1882, Will Reichard 375). Those raw values are then subtracted from canonical add values to produce the net gain and the tier badge.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);p=d['players'];print([(n,p[n].get('_finalAdjusted'),p[n].get('rankDerivedValue')) for n in ('Devon Witherspoon','Mason Graham','Malaki Starks','Will Reichard')])"
reproduction.expected: rows without a canonical stamp excluded from the comparison, as the add-side pool already does
reproduction.actual: [('Devon Witherspoon', 1935, None), ('Mason Graham', 1874, None), ('Malaki Starks', 1882, None), ('Will Reichard', 375, None)]

userImpact: The gating is one-sided -- an unstamped player can be DROPPED but never ADDED -- so the drop recommendations can be driven by numbers the canonical board refused to publish.

priorFinding.note: Mechanism confirmed against the current tree and the live payload; magnitude is smaller than the prior measurement (4 of 57 on team Jason vs 12 of 52 claimed for team Blaine). I did not reproduce the prior's claim that the headline tier flips -- on team Jason every visible tier is 'considering' either way, so that specific consequence is not-reproducible here.

whatWorks: The add-side pool does guard against this (rowHasNoRealRank + sourceCount).
rootCause: values.full is a union type across two payload views and two pipelines.
requiredRepair: Drop the fallback in rowValue and exclude unstamped rows from both sides.
